title: Check yourself: zoned and offset date-time

questions.stem: A choir's booking service receives its first rehearsal as the text 2026-10-20T19:00+02:00, parses it with ZonedDateTime.parse, and computes the next one with plusWeeks(1). The choir meets in Berlin, where the clocks go back from +02:00 to +01:00 on 25 October. At what time on Berlin's clocks does the service put the rehearsal of 27 October?

options.text: At 19:00, since the parsed value's zone carries the rules of a region that used +02:00 that evening
options.says: text without a region id parses to a zone that is the offset itself; no region and no rules are looked up

options.text: At 19:00, since the parsed value's zone is the fixed offset +02:00, which plusWeeks keeps
options.says: the value is 19:00+02:00, but Berlin is at +01:00 by then, so on Berlin's clocks that moment is 18:00

options.text: At 18:00, since the parsed value's zone is the fixed offset +02:00, which plusWeeks keeps
options.says: ZonedDateTime.parse of text with only an offset gives a ZoneOffset as the zone; 19:00+02:00 is 17:00 UTC, which is 18:00 in Berlin at +01:00

options.text: At 18:00, since the parsed value's zone carries the rules of a region that used +02:00 that evening
options.says: text without a region id parses to a zone that is the offset itself; no region and no rules are looked up

origin.section: A Zone Written as an Offset Has No Rules

questions.stem: A meter-reading job is configured for 01:30 local time in America/Denver. On 1 November 2026 Denver's clocks go from 02:00 back to 01:00, from -06:00 to -07:00. The scheduler computes that night's start with ZonedDateTime.of(LocalDateTime.of(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30), ZoneId.of("America/Denver")). When does the job start?

options.text: At the first 01:30, at -06:00, since a local time that happens twice is resolved to the offset in force before the change
options.says: in an overlap ZonedDateTime.of takes the earlier offset; withLaterOffsetAtOverlap() would pick the second 01:30

options.text: At the second 01:30, at -07:00, since a local time that happens twice is resolved to the offset in force after the change
options.says: ZonedDateTime.of resolves an overlap to the earlier offset; the second occurrence has to be picked, for example with withLaterOffsetAtOverlap()

options.text: It does not start, since ZonedDateTime.of throws DateTimeException for a local time that the zone's rules make ambiguous
options.says: ZonedDateTime.of resolves every valid local date-time without an exception; ofStrict is the call that throws for an invalid combination

options.text: It starts at 02:30, at -07:00, since ZonedDateTime.of moves a local time near a change later by the length of the change
options.says: moving later by the length of the change is what happens in a gap, where the time does not exist; 01:30 here exists twice

origin.section: Near a Clock Change a Local Time Can Be Missing or Doubled, and ZonedDateTime Picks One Without Telling You

questions.stem: A webinar is stored as 2026-10-29T16:00 in Europe/London, which is at +00:00 that day. A viewer in America/Chicago, which is at -05:00 that day, opens the event page, and the page shows the start from webinar.withZoneSameLocal(ZoneId.of("America/Chicago")). What does the viewer see, and when do they join if they follow it?

options.text: 16:00, and they join on time, since the result is the webinar's own start written with Chicago's offset
options.says: withZoneSameLocal keeps 16:00 and attaches Chicago's zone, which is a different moment, not the webinar's start

options.text: 16:00, and they join five hours late, since the result is a start five hours after the webinar's, written with Chicago's offset
options.says: 16:00 in Chicago at -05:00 is 21:00 UTC, five hours after the webinar's 16:00 UTC start

options.text: 11:00, and they join on time, since the result is the webinar's own start written with Chicago's offset
options.says: 11:00 is what withZoneSameInstant gives; withZoneSameLocal keeps the 16:00

options.text: 11:00, and they join five hours early, since the result is a start five hours before the webinar's, written with Chicago's offset
options.says: withZoneSameLocal keeps the time on the clock, so it shows 16:00, which is later, not earlier

origin.section: withZoneSameInstant Converts a Moment; withZoneSameLocal Moves It

questions.stem: A dental practice in America/Sao_Paulo, at -03:00 all year under current rules, stores each future appointment as an Instant computed when it is booked. In 2026 a patient books 10 March 2027 at 14:00. Suppose that before then the country brings back summer time, putting March 2027 at -02:00, and the server's JDK gets the new tzdata. What time does the reminder show when it converts the stored value with the zone?

options.text: 14:00, since the stored Instant is recomputed from the booked local time under the new rules
options.says: an Instant holds only seconds from 1970 and nothing recomputes it; the booked local time was not stored

options.text: 15:00, since the stored Instant is kept as it was and read with the new offset
options.says: 14:00 at -03:00 is 17:00 UTC; read at -02:00 that is 15:00, an hour after the time the patient booked

options.text: 14:00, since the stored Instant is kept as it was and read with the new offset
options.says: the moment is kept, but at -02:00 it shows an hour later on the clock: 15:00

options.text: 15:00, since the stored Instant is recomputed from the booked local time under the new rules
options.says: nothing recomputes a stored Instant; recomputing from the booked local time would give 14:00 again

origin.section: Store a Future Appointment as Local Time and Zone, and Work Out the Instant Late
